classification.difficultyReason: Directly read two labelled points with a common x-coordinate from each supplied graph; the required criterion is explicitly given.

content.prompt: The following relations are not functions. Write down the coordinates of two points on each graph that have the same $x$-coordinate.

spec.description: Unshaded circle centred at the origin with radius 3; positive axis arrows and four labelled intercepts. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: No selected answer points are marked.

answer.worked: The graph meets the $y$-axis at $(0,3)$ and $(0,-3)$. Both points have $x=0$, with different $y$-coordinates.

spec.description: Right-opening parabola with vertex (-1,0), crossings (0,1) and (0,-1), and continuation arrows on both branches. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: No selected answer points are marked.

answer.worked: The graph meets the $y$-axis at $(0,1)$ and $(0,-1)$. Both points have $x=0$, with different $y$-coordinates.

spec.description: Unshaded circle centred at (2,3), radius 2, tangent to the y-axis. Equal coordinate units; x ticks 2 and 4, y ticks 1, 3 and 5. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: No selected answer points or construction guides are marked.

answer.worked: The bottom and top of the circle are $(2,1)$ and $(2,5)$. Both points have $x=2$, with different $y$-coordinates.

spec.description: Vertical relation x=2 with continuation arrows at both ends, positive coordinate-axis arrows, ticks at -2 and 2 on both axes, and a right-angle square above the x-axis to the right of the relation. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: No selected answer points are marked.

answer.worked: Every point on the vertical line has $x=2$. For example, $(2,2)$ and $(2,-2)$ have the same $x$-coordinate and different $y$-coordinates.
